title: GPS-Q4-PURE: pure fourth-root copies and a complete integer-root source/time law

claims.statement: For every N>=2 and s in Z/NZ, n=ceil(log2N), the ONE GPS-Q4-PURE program in proof.md recovers the entire secret from independent ideal copies with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8>2/3. For n<2^256 it executes the explicit exhaustive finite branch; otherwise it computes u=ceil(n^(1/4)), ell=ceil(log2n), z=ceil(log2ell), b=ceil(3u^3(ell+2z+16)/2), m=ceil((n-1)/b), allocates the top-down constant-wide profile with positive r_i=b_i+1 and unit zero-width shortcuts, and recomputes all source/decoder/extraction and acquisition/fallback caps. On EVERY branch, including failed work, discarded copies, wrong labels and both aborts, charged time T is O(2^((3/4)n^(3/4)log2n+n^(3/4)(log2n)^(1/8))) with exact growth index3/4. Outside constants are absolute, independent of N,s and outcomes. Source, arithmetic, circuit generation, initialization, resets, measurement, preprocessing, full addressing and cleanup are paid jointly with the other resources and clean fraction0 for this same configuration.

For the same GPS-Q4-PURE algorithm and complete parameter rule in proof.md, the proved malformed-sample fractional guarantee is epsilon(n)=0: all Q acquired source copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, unconditional full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 1-2^-8 > 3/4 jointly with all four every-branch resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted, and this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
